The dust emission from the intergalactic medium in Stephan's Quintets can be explained by the heating of dust grains by the UV radiation of young stars.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the physical processes involved in dust emission in the interstellar medium (ISM), and in particular in the diffuse ISM.
the study of the dust emission in Stephan's Quintets (SQ), one of the most spectacular galaxy clusters known.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
dust collisional heating in the IGM gas is not negligible and that the dust emission is dominated by photons.
the dust emission of SQ is a mixture of collisional and radiative heating.
the dust emission in Stephan's Quintets is powered by photons, with a possible contribution by dust-gas collisional heating, in a ratio that is not easy to quantify.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the X-ray emitting IGM gas of Stephan's Quintets has a dust-to-gas ratio of ~10^-3 and a dust mass of 2.5x10^6 Msun.
we found that the X-ray emitting intergalactic shock is associated with a large scale dust emission feature that can be interpreted as a bow shock.
dust emission from the intergalactic medium of SQ is not dominated by the dust-gas collisions but rather by the dust-photons interactions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dust emission associated to the large scale interstellar medium of Stephan's Quintets, including that of the intergalactic shock, is not powered by dust-gass particle collisions but by photons.
the dust emission associated to the X-ray emitting IGM regions of SQ is not necessarily a sign of dust-gas particle heating.

the emission associated with the IGM shock and the group halo is dominated by the dust emission, and that the emission of the dust associated with the shock is more likely powered by photons than by collisions.
